Rashi on Eruvin 46a:11:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer - This is what we read:

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:11:2.hebrew: כל אשה שעברו עליה שלש עונות - דהיינו צ' יום, דעונה סתם לפריסת נדה משלשים יום לשלשים יום. וכל אשה שעברו עליה תשעים יום ולא ראתה — נסתלקו דמיה. ואם ראתה אחרי כן, אמרינן: השתא הוא דראתה דם, ולא מטמינן טהרות שנתעסק' בהן למפרע כשאר נשים שדמיהן מצויין, שמטמאות טהרות למפרע מעת לעת — כדאמר במס' נדה (דף ג.) דחיישינן שמא כותלי בית הרחם העמידוהו, ותנן (שם מ.) כל הנשים מטמאות בבית החיצון. ופליגי רבנן עליה, ואמרי דאין הפסקת ג' עונות סילוק אלא לזקנה שעברו עליה ג' עונות סמוך לזקנתה, אבל בילדה — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:11:2.english: Any woman who passed three cycles - That is, ninety days, as an ordinary cycle for the onset of menstruation is from thirty days to thirty days. And any woman who passed ninety days and did not see [blood], her blood has ceased. And if she saw [blood] after that, we say: It is [only] now that she saw blood, and we do not declare ritually impure the pure items she handled retroactively, as [is the rule for] other women whose blood is common, who impart ritual impurity to pure items retroactively for twenty-four hours — as [the Gemara] says in Tractate Niddah (folio 3a), that we are concerned lest the walls of the womb held it back, and we learned [in a mishna] (there, 40a): All women become ritually impure [as soon as blood reaches] the outer chamber. And the Rabbis disagree with him, and say that a cessation of three cycles is not [considered] a cessation except for an elderly woman who passed three cycles close to her old age, but in [the case of] a young woman, it is not.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:12:1.hebrew: כרבי אלעזר - וטיהר אף בילדה שעברו עליה ג' עונות:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:12:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Elazar - And he ruled [her] pure even in [the case of] a young woman for whom three [menstrual] cycles had passed.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:12:2.english: After he remembered - This implies that he remembered that he had not acted properly.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:12:3.hebrew: שעת הדחק - שני בצורת הוו, ואיכא הפסד טהרות:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:12:3.english: Exigent circumstances - They were years of drought, and there is a loss of ritually pure foods.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:13:1.hebrew: מאי כשנזכר - אילימא נזכר דאיתמר בפלוגתייהו הלכה כרבנן, וכשנעשה המעשה לא היה זכור, ועכשיו נזכר — אמאי לא אהדר עובדא:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:13:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "When he remembered" - If you say [it means] he remembered that it was stated regarding their dispute [that] the halakha is in accordance with the Rabbis, and when the incident occurred he did not remember, and now he remembered — why did he not reverse the act?

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:14:1.hebrew: אלא - האי דלא אהדר, משום דלא איתמר הלכתא לא כמר ולא כמר. ומאי "נזכר"? לאחר שנזכר דרבים פליגי עליה, דהוה ליה למיעבד כרבים, אמר: כדי הוא רבי אליעזר לסמוך עליו בשעת הדחק, ולא אהדר עובדא. הא לאו בשעת הדחק — לא! אלמא, אע"ג דמעת לעת גזירה דרבנן היא, בעי למיעבד כרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:14:1.english: Rather - The reason that he did not retract [his ruling] was because the halakha was not stated, neither like this Master nor like that Master. And what is [the meaning of] "he remembered"? After he remembered that many [Sages] disagree with him, so that he should have acted in accordance with the majority, he said: "Rabbi Eliezer is worthy to rely upon in exigent circumstances," and he did not reverse the action. But were it not in exigent circumstances, [he would] not [have done so]! Evidently, even though [the retroactive impurity of] a twenty-four-hour period is a rabbinic decree, one is required to act in accordance with the majority.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:16:1.hebrew: נוהגת שבעה - לרחיצה ולתכבוסת, ושלשים — לתספורת ולגיהוץ, מיום שנשמע לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:16:1.english: Is observed for seven [days] - For bathing and laundering; and thirty [days] — for haircutting and pressing, from the day it was heard by him.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:19:1.english: And he holds - Rabbi Yoḥanan [holds] like Shmuel.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:1:1.english: All the more so that they are nolad and forbidden - Even to move them in their place.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:2:1.hebrew: הרי הן כרגלי כל אדם - כיון דניידי, לא קנו שביתה. ואפילו הן של יחיד, אינן כרגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:2:1.english: They are like the feet of all people - Since they are in motion, they do not acquire a resting place; and even if they belong to an individual, they are not like his feet.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:3:1.english: Did you hear [it] explicitly - From Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:3:2.hebrew: או מכללא - דשמיע לך מיניה מילתא אחריתי, ודייקת מינה דכר' יוחנן בן נורי סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:3:2.english: Or by inference - That you heard another matter from him, and you inferred from it that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:4:1.hebrew: ומאי כללא - מאיזה כלל הוה ס"ד מעיקרא דשמעת ליה לר' יהושע בן לוי, דנימא מילתא דנידוק לה מינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:4:1.english: And what is the general rule - From what general rule did it initially enter [one's] mind that you heard from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, so that we should say [there was] a statement from which we could infer it?

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:4:2.hebrew: בעירוב - בכל משפטיו, ותחומין מהלכות עירובין הן:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:4:2.english: With regard to an eiruv - In all its laws; and [Sabbath] boundaries are among the laws of eiruvin.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:6:1.hebrew: בין לקולא - כגון אדם ישן, דאי לא קנה שביתה, לא נפיק מד' אמות:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:6:1.english: Whether this is a leniency - Such as a sleeping person, for if he did not acquire residence, he would not go out beyond four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:6:2.hebrew: לחומרא - כגון כלי הפקר: אי אמרת קונין שביתה, אסור להוליכן למקום שעירב זה המוצאן, אלא אלפים הוא דאית להו לכל רוח:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:6:2.english: As a stringency - Such as ownerless utensils: If you say [that] they acquire residence, it is forbidden to carry them to the place where this [person] who finds them made an eiruv; rather, they have only two thousand [cubits] in each direction.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:6:3.hebrew: קמ"ל כדברי המיקל - באדם הוא דהלכתא כוותיה, דכיון דניעור קנה, ישן נמי קנה. אבל בכלים — לית הלכתא כוותיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:6:3.english: He teaches us in accordance with the lenient opinion - It is with regard to a person that the halakha is in accordance with him, for since an awake person acquires [residence], a sleeping person also acquires [residence]. But with regard to utensils, the halakha is not in accordance with him.

Rashi on Eruvin 46a:8:1.hebrew: אבל יחיד במקום רבים - כגון ר' יוחנן בן נורי, דפליגי רבנן עליה — אימא: לית הלכתא כוותיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 46a:8:1.english: But an individual against many - Such as Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, with whom the Rabbis disagree — you might say that the halakha is not in accordance with him.

Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:14:1.hebrew: לסמוך עליו בשעת הדחק - פי' הקונטרס דשנת בצורת הוה, ואיכא הפסד טהרות. ואי אפשר לומר כן, דבדחק כה"ג אפי' רבנן מודים — כדאמר בפ"ק דנדה (ד' ט:): "אין שעת הדחק ראיה", ומפרש התם: מאי שעת הדחק? שנת בצורת הוה. ואיכא דאמרי: דטהרות אפיש ועבוד, וחשו רבנן להפסד טהרות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:14:1.english: To rely upon him in exigent circumstances - Rashi explained that it was a year of drought and there is a loss of ritually pure items. And it is impossible to say so, for in an exigency of this sort, even the Rabbis concede — as the Gemara states in the first chapter of Niddah (9b): "Exigent circumstances are no proof," and the Gemara explains there: What were the exigent circumstances? It was a year of drought. And some say: That ritually pure items were plentiful and already prepared, and the Rabbis were concerned for the loss of ritually pure items.

Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:19:1.hebrew: דאמר שמואל הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל - אפילו ביחיד במקום רבים, נראה דלעולם הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל; ו"חוץ מזו" לאו למעוטי שאר מקומות דאבל קאמר, כדקאמר: "אבילות הוא דאקילו ביה רבנן". וכן מוכיח בהדיא פרק בתרא דמו"ק (דף יט:) גבי אבא שאול ורבנן, גבי קובר את מתו ג' ימים לפני הרגל; וגבי בא ממקום קרוב, פלוגתא דרשב"ג ורבנן (דף כב.). וא"ת: כיון דאפי' יחיד במקום רבים אמר שמואל הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל, למה ליה לשמואל למיפסק בפרק בתרא דמו"ק (דף כד.) כרשב"ג, דאמר ר"ה ויום הכפורים כרגלים? ויש לומר: דקמ"ל אפי' ביחיד במקום רבים, כדאמר לעיל. ונראה: אפי' ביום ראשון של אבילות דהוי דאורייתא, כדאמר בה"ג, דהלכה כדברי המיקל באבל — מידי דהוי כהלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב, דמשמע לעיל דאפילו הוי דאורייתא הלכה כדברי המיקל, מדקאמר: "מכדי עירובין דרבנן, מה לי יחיד במקום וכו'", משמע דאי הוה דאורייתא ניחא דצריכי. וכן מוכח בפ' יש בכור (בכורות דף מט.) גבי פלוגתא דר"ע ורבנן, דאמר רב אשי: הכל מודים לענין אבילות דיום ל' כשלפניו, דאמר שמואל הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל, ואפילו ביום ראשון אינו נוהג אבילות. וזה לשון ה"ג: "היכא דשכיב שכיבא ביום טוב ראשון או ביום טוב שני, או בחולו של מועד, או בי"ט ראשון של יום טוב אחרון — אינו נוהג אבילות עד דנפקי יומא טבא כולהו; אבל יומא בתרא דרבנן, מסלק סליק למנין ז', אבל אבילות לא נהיג ביה כלל. אבל שכיב שכיבא בי"ט שני של י"ט אחרון, כיון דעיקר אבילות יום ראשון — נהיג ביה אבילות וסליק למנין ז', דהכי אסמכוה רבנן דעיקר אבילות יום ראשון הוא, דכתיב: 'ואכלתי חטאת היום היום אסור ולמחר מותר', וכתיב: 'ואחריתה כיום מר'. וכיון דיום ראשון דאבילות דאורייתא, ויום טוב אחרון ספיקא דרבנן — אתי עשה ודאי דאורייתא דיחיד וחייל על עשה ספק דרבים דרבנן". והא דאמרינן בכתובות (דף ד'.): "מכניסין את המת לחדר ונוהג ז' ימי המשתה ואחר כך נוהג ז' ימי אבילות", אלמא דלא דחי יומא קמא דאבילות מועד דרבנן — שמא מועד דחתן עדיף טפי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:19:1.english: As Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion with regard to mourning — Even [in a case of] an individual [ruling leniently] against many, it appears that the halakha is always in accordance with the lenient opinion with regard to mourning; and [when Rabbi Yoḥanan said] "except for this one," he did not mean to exclude the other cases of mourning, as [the Gemara soon] states: "It is with regard to mourning that the Sages were lenient." And so [the Gemara] explicitly proves in the final chapter of Moed Katan (19b) regarding Abba Shaul and the Rabbis, in the case of one who buries his dead three days before the festival; and regarding one who arrives from a nearby place, [in] the dispute between Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis (22a). And if you say: Since Shmuel said [that] the halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion with regard to mourning even [in a case of] an individual against many, why did Shmuel need to rule in the final chapter of Moed Katan (24a) in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said [that] Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are like the pilgrimage festivals [to annul mourning]? And one can say: It comes to teach us [that the rule applies] even [in a case of] an individual against many, as was stated above. And it appears [that] even on the first day of mourning, which is biblical, as the Halakhot Gedolot says, the halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion with regard to mourning — just as it is with "the halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion with regard to an eruv," which implied above that even if it were biblical, the halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion, from the fact that [the Gemara] said: "After all, eruvin are rabbinic; what difference does it make to me [whether it is] an individual against [an individual or an individual against many]...", which implies that if it were biblical, it would be well understood that they are needed. And so it is proven in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49a) regarding the dispute between Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis, where Rav Ashi said: Everyone agrees with regard to mourning that the thirtieth day is like that which precedes it, for Shmuel said [that] the halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion with regard to mourning, and even on the first day he does not observe mourning. And this is the text of the Halakhot Gedolot: "Where someone's deceased relative died on the first day of Yom Tov, or on the second day of Yom Tov, or on Ḥol HaMoed, or on the first day of the final Yom Tov [i.e., Shemini Atzeret] — he does not observe mourning until all the festive days have ended; but the last day [i.e., Simchat Torah], which is rabbinic, does count toward the tally of seven [days of mourning], although he does not observe mourning on it at all. But if one's deceased relative died on the second day of the final Yom Tov, since the essence of mourning is the first day, he observes mourning on it and it counts toward the tally of seven; for so did the Rabbis derive from a verse that the essence of mourning is the first day, as it is written: 'And I ate sin offering today; today it is forbidden, but tomorrow it is permitted' [Leviticus 10:19], and it is written: 'And the end thereof as a bitter day' [Amos 8:10]. And since the first day of mourning is biblical, and the final Yom Tov is a rabbinic doubt [arising from the calendar], the certain biblical positive commandment of an individual comes and takes effect over the doubtful rabbinic positive commandment of the community." And as for that which we say in Ketubot (4a): "They bring the deceased into a room, and he observes the seven days of the [wedding] celebration, and afterwards he observes the seven days of mourning" — from which it follows that the first day of mourning does not override a rabbinic festival — perhaps the festival of a groom is superior [i.e., has greater weight than an ordinary rabbinic holiday].

Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:1:1.hebrew: כל שכן דהוי ליה נולד ואסיר - ואע"ג דמשקין בפירי נמי אמרינן בפסחים (דף לג:) דמבלע בליעי, אפ"ה לא מתסרי משום נולד אי לא גזרינן שמא יסחוט; דמים בעבים בליעי טפי, ואינה ניכרין כמו משקין בפירי. ואפילו לא היו ניכרין משקין בפירי כלל, לא חשיבי נולד, כיון דמעיקרא נמי הוי אוכל — אוכלא דאיפרת הוא. וא"ת: ולימא הא רבי שמעון היא, דלית ליה מוקצה ולית ליה נולד, כדאיתא בריש ביצה (דף ב.)? וי"ל: דבנולד כה"ג, דדבר חדש שלא בא לעולם כל עיקר, מודה רבי שמעון. וכן באפר כירה שהוסק ביום טוב, נראה דמודה ר"ש דאסור לכסות בו, אא"כ ראוי לצלות בו ביצה, כדאמר בפרק קמא דביצה (דף ח.):
Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:1:1.english: All the more so should it be [considered] nolad and prohibited - And even though regarding liquids in fruit we also say in Pesachim (33b) that they are absorbed, even so, they are not prohibited on account of nolad were we not to decree [a prohibition] lest one squeeze [them]; for water in the clouds is more absorbed, and [its presence] is not discernible like liquids in fruit. And even if liquids in fruit were not discernible at all, they would not be considered nolad, since initially [before oozing out] they were also food — it is [merely] food that has separated. And if you say: But let [the Gemara] say that this [baraita] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Shimon, who does not hold of [the prohibition of] muktzeh and does not hold of nolad, as is found at the beginning of Beitzah (2a)? And one can say [in reply]: In [a case of] nolad of this kind, where it is a new entity that had not come into the world at all, Rabbi Shimon concedes [that it is prohibited]. And similarly, regarding the ash of a stove that was heated on the Festival, it appears that Rabbi Shimon concedes that it is prohibited to cover [the blood of a slaughtered animal or bird] with it, unless it is fit to roast an egg upon it, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Beitzah (8a).

Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:6:1.hebrew: נהרות המושכין - פ"ה: אפי' הן של יחיד. ונראה שדקדק, דאי הוה של רבים דווקא — מאי איריא נהרות? אפי' מים מכונסים נמי אמרי' לעיל: "כרגלי הממלא", והיינו "כרגלי כל אדם" דהכא, כדפרישי' לעיל דהכל אחד. וכן מוכח בפרק בתרא דביצה (דף לט.) דבשל יחיד מיירי, דפריך מהך דהכא אמתני' דהתם דקתני: "בור של יחיד — כרגלי היחיד". ומיהו שם לא פירש רש"י "כרגלי הממלא" ו"כרגלי כל אדם" בענין אחד. ור"ת מפרש: אפילו מיירי בשל רבים, מדקדק שפיר, דדווקא משום דניידי לא קנו שביתה, אבל מכונסים — דקנו שביתה — יש להם אלפים אמה לכל רוח, כרבי יוחנן בן נורי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:6:1.english: Flowing rivers - Rashi explained: Even [if] they belong to an individual. And it appears that he deduced [this because] if it were specifically [dealing with water] belonging to the public, why specifically [mention] flowing rivers? Even gathered water we also said above [is] "like the feet of the one who draws [it]," and that is [the same as] "like the feet of all people" [stated] here, as we explained above that it is all one [and the same]. And it is also proven in the last chapter of Beitzah (39a) that it is dealing with [water] belonging to an individual, for [the Gemara there] objects from this [baraita] here against the Mishnah there, which teaches: "A cistern belonging to an individual is like the feet of the individual." However, there, Rashi did not explain "like the feet of the one who draws" and "like the feet of all people" in the same manner. And Rabbeinu Tam explains: Even [if] it is dealing with [water] belonging to the public, [the baraita] precisely specifies [flowing rivers], for specifically because they are in motion, they did not acquire residence, but gathered [waters] — which do acquire residence — have two thousand cubits in every direction, in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:6:2.hebrew: הוה אמינא בין לקולא בין לחומרא - הוה ליה למימר דאיצטריך הלכה כדברי המיקל לפסוק הלכה בכל מקומות, אלא דניחא ליה למימר דאפילו להך מילתא גופה איצטריך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:6:2.english: "I would have said, whether for a leniency or for a stringency" - [Rabbi Zeira] could have said that [the statement] "the halakha is in accordance with the lenient opinion" was necessary to determine the halakha in all [other] places, but it was preferable to him to say that it was necessary even for this matter itself.

Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:6:3.hebrew: קמ"ל הלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב - דלענין אדם, הלכה כרבי יוחנן בן נורי דקני שביתה; ולענין כלים, הלכה כרבנן דלא קנו שביתה, והרי הן כרגלי כל אדם. ולא הוי תרי קולי דסתרי אהדדי, דקיימא לן כרבנן דאמרי: אין חפצי הפקר קונין שביתה, וישן היינו טעמא — הואיל וניעור קני, ישן נמי קני, כדפ"ה. ואפילו אם לא היה משמעינן רבי יהושע בן לוי אלא "הלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב" לחוד, הוה משמע מדבריו דהלכתא כדברי שניהם להקל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 46a:6:3.english: He teaches us: "The halakha is in accordance with the lenient [opinion] with regard to an eiruv" - That regarding a person, the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri that he acquires residence; and regarding utensils, the halakha is in accordance with the Rabbis that they do not acquire residence, and behold, they are like the feet of any person. And this is not [a case of] two leniencies that contradict each other, for we hold in accordance with the Rabbis, who say that ownerless objects do not acquire residence, and [as for] a sleeping person, this is the reason: since an awake [person] acquires [residence], a sleeping [person] also acquires [residence], as the Kuntres explained. And even if Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi had taught us only "the halakha is in accordance with the one who is lenient regarding an eiruv" alone, it would have been understood from his words that the halakha is in accordance with the words of both of them to be lenient.
